4 Ἐνήστευσεν τὸ κῆτος ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, ὅτε ἐδέξατο τὸν Ἰωνᾶν ἐν τοῖς τῆς
κοιλίας ταμιείοις· ἔχον γὰρ τὸν προφήτην ὡς παραθήκην, ἐπεδείξατο τὸ τῆς

κοιλίας ταμιείοις, ἀπεκατέστησεν σώαν τὴν παραθήκην, παραδοὺς τῷ

ἠθέλησεν, ἐκώλυσεν τὸν ὑετὸν καί, ὅτε ἠθέλησεν, ἤνεγκεν αὐτὸν διὰ νηστειῶν καὶ

5 Ἐνήστευ<σεν> ὁ σωτὴρ ἡμ<ῶν> τεσσαράκοντα ἡμέρας καὶ τὸν διάβολον
κατῄσχυνεν, ὁ ἁμαρτίαν μὴ ποιήσας μηδὲ δόλος εὑρέθη ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτοῦ.
Ἐνήστευσεν δὲ τύπον ἡμῖν διδοὺς ὅτι διὰ νηστειῶν δυνάμεθα τυχεῖν ἐξιλασμοῦ

thought_title: Fasting tames beasts, fire, sea, and sin
orientation: Hesychius is cataloguing biblical examples of fasting's power, moving from Daniel's lions to the three youths, Jonah, David, Elijah, Jesus, and the apostles.
pass_a_gloss: the mouths of the lions. [It] fasted the fire in the furnace and [it] did not use the fellow-slaves for food, but having fasted [it] leaped out of the furnace, having yielded to the three because of the fourth. [It] fasted the sea-monster in the sea, when [it] received Jonah in the inner chambers of the belly; for having the prophet as a deposit, [it] displayed the sign of fasting. For instead of a ship to the shipwrecked [man] having become, [it] carried the stranger through sea and depth and great fear and, in order that [it] might not destroy the stranger in the inner chambers of the belly, [it] restored safe the deposit, having handed [it] over to the master who had deposited [it]. [He] fasted David and, through fasting and repentance, [God] forgave him the sin of the wife of Uriah. [He] fasted Elijah forty days and the keys of the heavens [he] received and, when [he] wished, [he] prevented the rain and, when [he] wished, [he] brought it through fastings and prayers. [He] fasted our Savior forty days and the devil [he] put to shame, the [one] sin not having done nor deceit was found in the mouth of him. [He] fasted and a model to us giving that through fastings we are able to obtain propitiation of sins. Let us fast therefore, beloved, a fast pure about which says the apostle James that "religion pure this is: to visit" brothers "in the affliction of them, spotless themselves to keep from the world." [He] fasted Joshua the [son] of Nun and to the sun and to the moon [he] commanded. The apostles, nothing having on earth, to bind and to loose authority [they] received and [it] is fulfilled in them the [thing] said: "as nothing having and all things possessing." Peter for, [he] says, and John about hour ninth went up into the temple to pray. And a certain [man] lame from womb of mother of him being was sitting, who never walked. This [man] was expecting to receive something from the apostles.

choices.why: Keeps the personification of the fire as the subject of the verb 'fasted', matching the source's rhetorical pattern of inanimate or non-human subjects fasting.
Uses the glossary term for παραθήκη, preserving the financial metaphor of something entrusted and returned intact.
Renders κλεῖς literally as 'keys' and οὐρανῶν as 'heavens' to preserve the image of authority over rain.
Keeps the theological term 'propitiation' for ἐξιλασμός, distinguishing it from simple forgiveness (συγχώρησις) used earlier for David.
Renders the infinitive pair literally, preserving the rabbinic legal metaphor of authority.
Keeps the literal phrase for congenital lameness, matching the biblical idiom.

bible_refs.note: God shut the mouths of the lions
the fourth figure in the furnace with the three youths
Jonah in the belly of the sea monster
David's sin concerning Uriah's wife forgiven
who did not commit sin nor was deceit found in his mouth
pure religion is this: to visit brothers in their affliction, to keep themselves unstained from the world

pass_b_english: the mouths of the lions. The fire fasted in the furnace and did not use its fellow servants for food, but having fasted it leaped out of the furnace, yielding to the three because of the fourth (Daniel 3:25).

The sea monster fasted in the sea when it received Jonah into the chambers of its belly. For holding the prophet as a deposit, it displayed the sign of fasting. Becoming a ship for the shipwrecked man, it carried the stranger through sea and depth and great fear, and so that it might not destroy the stranger in the chambers of its belly, it restored the deposit intact, handing it over to the master who had entrusted it (Jonah 2:1-10).

David fasted, and through fasting and repentance God forgave him the sin concerning Uriah's wife (2 Samuel 12:13). Elijah fasted forty days and received the keys of the heavens, and when he wished he withheld the rain, and when he wished he brought it through fastings and prayers (1 Kings 17:1; 18:45).

Our Savior fasted forty days and put the devil to shame—he who committed no sin, nor was deceit found in his mouth (Matthew 4:2; 1 Peter 2:22). He fasted to give us a pattern, that through fastings we are able to obtain propitiation of sins.

Let us fast, then, beloved, a pure fast, about which the apostle James says: “Pure religion is this: to visit brothers in their affliction, to keep themselves unstained from the world” (James 1:27). Joshua son of Nun fasted and commanded the sun and the moon (Joshua 10:12-13).

The apostles, having nothing on earth, received authority to bind and to loose, and what was said is fulfilled in them: “as having nothing and possessing all things” (2 Corinthians 6:10). For Peter, it says, and John went up to the temple at the ninth hour to pray. And a certain man lame from his mother's womb was sitting there, who had never walked. He was expecting to receive something from the apostles (Acts 3:1-3).
notes: Ἐνήστευ<σεν> and ἡμ<ῶν> are restored from context; the angle brackets mark editorial supplements in the source text.

last_rejected.quote: The fire fasted in the furnace and did not use its fellow servants for food
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἐνήστευσεν τὸ πῦρ ἐν τῇ καμίνῳ καὶ οὐκ ἐχρήσατο τοῖς συνδούλοις εἰς βρῶσιν
last_rejected.why: English hides that 'fellow servants' refers to the three young men, making the fire's personification unclear.
last_rejected.fix: The fire fasted in the furnace and did not make food of its fellow servants, the three young men.
last_rejected.ruling: συνδούλοις = 'fellow servants'; English renders the word correctly. The Daniel context makes the reference clear to readers.

last_rejected.quote: yielding to the three because of the fourth
last_rejected.source_quote: παραχωρῆσαν τοῖς τρισὶν διὰ τὸν τέταρτον
last_rejected.why: English reverses agency: the fire yielded/gave way, not the fourth yielding to the three.
last_rejected.fix: giving way to the three on account of the fourth.
last_rejected.ruling: παραχωρῆσαν (fire yielded) is correctly rendered 'yielding'; English preserves agency accurately.

last_rejected.quote: Becoming a ship for the shipwrecked man
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἀντὶ γὰρ νηὸς τῷ ναυαγήσαντι γενόμενον
last_rejected.why: English inverts the Greek: the monster became a ship for the shipwrecked man, not 'becoming a ship' as subject.
last_rejected.fix: For instead of a ship, having become one to the shipwrecked man, it carried the stranger...
last_rejected.ruling: Ἀντὶ νηὸς γενόμενον = 'becoming a ship'; English correctly conveys the monster became a ship for the shipwrecked man.

last_rejected.quote: He fasted to give us a pattern
last_rejected.why: Missing 'but/and' (δὲ) and the participial force: 'fasting while giving' or 'fasted, giving us a pattern'.
last_rejected.fix: And he fasted, giving us a pattern, that through fastings we are able to obtain propitiation of sins.
last_rejected.ruling: δὲ is a mild connective; 'to give us a pattern' captures τύπον ἡμῖν διδοὺς adequately. Minor stylistic preference only.

last_rejected.quote: to keep themselves unstained from the world
last_rejected.source_quote: ἀσπίλους ἑαυτοὺς τηρεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ κόσμου
last_rejected.why: James commands 'keep oneself' (middle), not 'themselves' as third person; 'themselves' obscures it's direct address.
last_rejected.fix: to keep oneself unstained from the world.
last_rejected.ruling: ἑαυτοὺς τηρεῖν is standard reflexive; 'themselves' correctly renders the Greek middle form in context.

last_rejected.source_quote: Ἐνήστευσεν τὸ κῆτος...ἀπεκατέστησεν σώαν τὴν παραθήκην
last_rejected.why: The citation Jonah 2:1-10 covers Jonah's prayer from the fish, not the fish's fasting or deposit imagery; better Jonah 1:17-2:10.
last_rejected.ruling: Jonah 2:1-10 (LXX) reasonably covers the fish narrative; the suggested range is a minor preference, not a major error.
